newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran students protest again at German embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran students protest again at German embassy.

text.p: More than 1,000 Iranian students marched to the German embassy in Tehran on Monday to protest against a Berlin court verdict accusing Iran's leaders of ordering political killings, witnesses said.

The students, from high schools for children of soldiers killed in the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war, chanted "Death to America", "Death to Israel" and slogans denouncing the court's judge as a servant of Iran's arch-enemies.
About two dozen policemen guarded the embassy and there were no incidents, said the witnesses, who spoke to Reuters by telephone.

Iranian Intelligence (internal security) Minister Ali Fallahiyan, quoted by the daily Jomhuri Eslami, accused Germany of holding Kazam Darabi hostage and setting up the Berlin trial to pressure Iran to help in locating a missing Israeli airman.

He was referring to an Iranian sentenced to life imprisonment by the court which also jailed three Lebanese and accused top Tehran leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran denies any involvement.
Fallahiyan said German and Iranian security agencies had long cooperated in the fight against "drugs and terrorism".
"But lately the Germans were under heavy pressure from the Zionist regime (Israel), so that they were seeking advantages from us as a price for continued cooperation," Fallahiyan said.

Fallahiyan was referring to Ron Arad, the Israeli airman missing since his plane was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. Israel has said it believed Arad was being held in Iran. Tehran has denied knowing his whereabouts.
"They (Germans) also took hostage an Iranian citizen, Kazem Darabi, and demanded the release of the Israeli pilot by Iran," Fallahiyan said.

Germany last year issued an arrest warrant for Fallahiyan, the only official accused by name by the Berlin court which also ruled that the country's state president and religious leader were among officials behind the assassinations.
